checklist.step: Scope the market entry to exact writing company, state and lines
actions: Take the signed market-entry request from the Chief Underwriting Officer and the Insurance Product Manager and open a new market-entry record in the licensing register.
Record the writing company legal name, NAIC company code, FEIN, state of domicile, target state (North Carolina), target first-write date and the products to be sold.

Translate each product into the state's own lines of authority wording — for North Carolina, the Chapter 58 kinds of insurance (e.g. fire and casualty, life, accident and health) rather than the internal product name.
Ask the Insurance Product Manager for the premium volume forecast and whether business is direct, agency or program, because it drives which UCAA exhibits are required.
Attach the signed market-entry request to the record and set status to 'Scoped'.
checklist.done: the record names one writing company, one state and an explicit list of statutory lines of authority with a target first-write date.

checklist.step: Check whether an in-force Certificate of Authority already covers the state and line
actions: Open the CoA register and filter on the writing company and North Carolina; read the CoA number, issue date, status and the lines of authority as granted.
Independently confirm the register against the source: look the company up in NAIC iSite+ (Company Demographics / State Licensing) and in the NCDOI 'Company Search' on the department's website.
Compare the granted lines to the target line list and mark each target line COVERED, PARTIAL (line granted but sub-line or kind not) or NOT COVERED.
Where the register and the state record disagree, treat the state record as authoritative and raise a data-correction ticket to the Regulatory Affairs Manager the same day.
Hand the gap list to the Regulatory Affairs Manager; if every line is COVERED the entry needs no UCAA filing and moves straight to the pre-write gate step.
checklist.done: each target line is marked covered or not covered against the state's own record, and any register-vs-state discrepancy has a correction ticket.

checklist.step: Read North Carolina's current admission requirements before building anything
actions: Read N.C. Gen. Stat. Chapter 58, Article 7 on admission of foreign insurers, and the article covering the kinds of insurance being requested, on the NC General Assembly site.
Open the NAIC UCAA page and download the current North Carolina State Specific Requirements sheet plus the Expansion Application instructions and checklist.

List every North Carolina deviation from the uniform package: additional forms, notarization, number of copies, retaliatory fee basis and whether electronic submission through the UCAA Filing Application is accepted.

Print the statute sections and the State Specific Requirements sheet to PDF, name them nc-admission-requirements-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file them in the market-entry folder as the evidence behind the package design.
Email the NCDOI Company Admissions contact any question the instructions leave open and log the question, date asked and answer received.
checklist.done: a dated capture of the statute and the state's UCAA State Specific Requirements sits in the folder, with every state deviation listed.

checklist.step: Fix the UCAA application type and confirm the state accepts it
actions: Choose the application type: Expansion (already admitted somewhere, seeking a new state), Primary (seeking redomestication or a first licence in a new domicile) or Corporate Amendments (name change, merger, redomestication, change of lines on an existing CoA).
For this entry confirm Expansion applies because the company holds an in-force CoA in its domiciliary state and is adding North Carolina.
Check on the NAIC UCAA page that North Carolina accepts that application type and note whether it participates in the Expansion Application Review (peer review) programme.
Where the change is to an existing CoA rather than a new state, switch to the Corporate Amendments Application and pull that form set instead.
Write the chosen application type and the reason onto the market-entry record.
checklist.done: the application type is chosen, evidenced against the state's UCAA participation, and recorded with its reason.

checklist.step: Test capital, surplus and RBC against the state's admission minimums
actions: Pull the most recent filed Annual Statement and the latest quarterly for the writing company: capital paid up, gross paid-in and contributed surplus, and surplus as regards policyholders from Page 3 (Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds).
Read North Carolina's minimum capital and surplus for each requested kind of insurance from Chapter 58 and the State Specific Requirements sheet, and sum the requirement across the requested lines.
Compute the headroom = surplus as regards policyholders minus the aggregate state minimum, and compute the RBC ratio (Total Adjusted Capital / Authorized Control Level) from the RBC filing.

Where headroom is thin or the RBC ratio would draw a question, get the Chief Financial Officer to confirm in writing that a capital contribution will be made before submission, and attach the commitment.
Record the tested figures, the source statement date and the conclusion on the market-entry record.
checklist.done: tested capital, surplus and RBC figures with their statement date beat the aggregate state minimum, or a written capital commitment is attached.

checklist.step: Build the UCAA Expansion package item by item
actions: Open the UCAA Expansion Application checklist and create one folder per numbered item so nothing is assembled from memory.

Assemble the core items: the Application form and Uniform Application Checklist, certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws, Certificate of Compliance/Good Standing from the domiciliary regulator dated within the state's freshness window, Certificate of Deposit, Corporate Amendments history and the Plan of Operation with pro-forma financials for the state.

Draft the Plan of Operation specifically for North Carolina: products, distribution channels, territory, projected premium by line for three years, underwriting and claims handling arrangements, and reinsurance program.
Mark every checklist item Not Started / In Progress / Complete with an owner and a due date backed off the submission date.
Have the Regulatory Affairs Manager review the package against the checklist before anything is uploaded.
checklist.done: every numbered UCAA Expansion checklist item is Complete with a named owner, or is explicitly marked not applicable with the state instruction that says so.

checklist.step: Collect NAIC Biographical Affidavits with third-party verification
actions: List every officer, director and key functional manager the state requires an affidavit from, taken from the current board roster and the officer list in the Jurat page of the Annual Statement.

Send each person the current NAIC Biographical Affidavit (UCAA Form 11) and require full employment history with no unexplained gaps, all names used, and disclosure of criminal, regulatory and bankruptcy matters.

Have each affidavit notarised and order the third-party background verification report from an NAIC-accepted vendor, since states generally require the verification to be dated within the preceding 12 months.
Review every affirmative disclosure with Regulatory Counsel before submission and prepare a written explanation letter for each one.
File affidavits and verification reports in the package folder and record the affidavit date so the 12-month freshness can be re-tested if the filing stalls.
checklist.done: a notarised affidavit and a third-party verification report dated within 12 months exists for every required officer and director, with counsel-cleared explanations for every disclosure.

checklist.step: Execute the Uniform Consent to Service of Process and appoint the statutory agent
actions: Prepare the UCAA Uniform Consent to Service of Process (Form 12) naming the North Carolina Commissioner of Insurance as attorney for service, and the officer authorised by board resolution to sign it.
Confirm a board or written-consent resolution authorises the officer to execute the consent and the application, and attach the certified resolution.
Route for signature and notarisation through DocuSign with the notary workflow, then obtain the wet-signed original where the state requires originals rather than scans.
Register the company with the NC Secretary of State as a foreign corporation and record the registered agent name and address, since admission requires the corporate registration to be in place.
File the executed consent, the resolution and the Secretary of State registration certificate in the package folder.
checklist.done: an executed, notarised consent to service of process and a current NC Secretary of State foreign registration are both in the package.

checklist.step: Assemble the financial and actuarial exhibits the state will read
actions: Attach the two most recent audited statutory financial statements with the independent auditor's opinion, and the most recent quarterly statement.
Attach the Statement of Actuarial Opinion signed by the Appointed Actuary and, where the state asks for it, the Actuarial Opinion Summary.

Attach the holding company registration statement (Form B) and the latest Form F enterprise risk report as filed with the domiciliary regulator, plus an organisational chart showing ultimate controlling person.
Attach the current RBC filing and the five-year historical data page from the Annual Statement.
Have the Appointed Actuary confirm in writing that the reserve position supports the lines being requested in North Carolina and file the confirmation.
checklist.done: audited statutory statements, actuarial opinion, holding-company filings and RBC are attached and internally consistent with the figures cited in the Plan of Operation.

checklist.step: Arrange the statutory deposit and obtain the certificate of deposit
actions: Read the North Carolina deposit requirement from the State Specific Requirements sheet and the NAIC Statutory Deposit requirements, noting the amount, the eligible securities and whether the deposit is held by the state or by the domiciliary state on a trusteed basis.
Instruct the custodian to place or reallocate the securities and obtain the custodian's certificate showing CUSIP, par value, market value and the state named as beneficiary.
Obtain the Certificate of Deposit from the domiciliary regulator where a domiciliary-held deposit satisfies the requirement.
Record the deposit amount, securities and review date in the licensing register so the deposit can be re-tested at each annual continuation.
File the custodian certificate and the regulator certificate in the package folder.
checklist.done: the deposit meets the stated North Carolina amount and a dated certificate naming the state is in the package and recorded in the register.

checklist.step: Pay the fees and submit the filing through the UCAA Filing Application
actions: Compute the fee: the state's application and licence fee plus any retaliatory fee measured against what the state of domicile would charge a North Carolina insurer, using the state's fee schedule.
Raise the payment through Accounts Payable with the correct payee and reference, and obtain proof of payment or the EFT confirmation.

Log in to the NAIC UCAA Filing Application, create the Expansion filing for North Carolina, upload each checklist item into its numbered slot and complete the Uniform Application Checklist showing the location of every item.
Submit, then capture the submission confirmation, the filing identifier and the submission date, and screenshot the submitted item list.
Set the market-entry record to 'Submitted' with the submission date and calculate the expected review window (60 days from a complete filing) as the first follow-up date.
checklist.done: the filing is submitted with proof of fee payment, a captured submission confirmation and a diarised follow-up date.

checklist.step: Clear deficiency letters and state interrogatories inside the response window
actions: Log every NCDOI deficiency letter or interrogatory as a tracker issue on the day it arrives with the state's stated response due date.

Break each letter into individual questions and assign each to the owning function — Statutory Reporting for financials, Corporate Secretary for affidavits, Legal for corporate documents, Product for the Plan of Operation.
Draft one consolidated response letter answering each numbered point in the state's own order, attach the supporting exhibits and have Regulatory Counsel review it before it leaves.
Upload the response into the UCAA filing and record the upload date; where an extension is needed, request it in writing before the due date rather than after.
Keep the tracker issue open until the state confirms the point is cleared.
checklist.done: every deficiency point has a dated, counsel-reviewed written response filed on or before the state's due date, and the state has confirmed clearance.

checklist.step: Record the issued Certificate of Authority and its lines of authority
actions: On receipt of the CoA, read the certificate itself and record CoA number, effective date, expiry or continuation basis, and the lines of authority exactly as the state worded them.
Scan the certificate and attach the image to the state row in the CoA register; do not record from the covering email.
Re-verify the entry against NAIC iSite+ and the NCDOI company search so the register matches the public record.
Update the enterprise state/line matrix and publish the change to Underwriting, Distribution and Policy Administration in writing.
Load the annual continuation date and the deposit review date into the register calendar with reminders.
checklist.done: the register carries the certificate image, the CoA number, the effective date and the state's own line wording, verified against the public record.

checklist.step: Release the state/line write switch only after the CoA is in force
actions: Keep the North Carolina state/line combination disabled in the product availability configuration and in the rating engine until the CoA effective date is recorded in the register.
On release, set the earliest bind date on the state/line to the CoA effective date, never earlier, and confirm quoting and binding are blocked for any line not on the certificate.
Run a bind test in the pre-production environment for one covered line and one deliberately uncovered line, and confirm the uncovered line is refused.
Notify Underwriting and Distribution of the exact date business may be written and of the lines that remain closed.
Record the configuration change reference and the tester's name on the market-entry record.
checklist.done: binding is enabled for the state only from the CoA effective date, uncovered lines are demonstrably refused, and the test evidence is on the record.

checklist.step: File the evidence and arm the ongoing CoA maintenance calendar
actions: Move the complete market-entry folder — statute captures, UCAA package, affidavits, deposit certificates, deficiency correspondence, the CoA image and the configuration release note — into the compliance evidence repository under Company Licensing / North Carolina.
Apply the retention label of CoA life plus 7 years after withdrawal so the record survives any future exit from the state.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by writing company, NAIC company code, state and CoA number.

Create the recurring maintenance tasks: annual continuation fee and renewal, deposit adequacy review, and a Corporate Amendments trigger list (name change, merger, redomestication, change in lines or control).
Close the market-entry record with the Head of Compliance's attestation that the state/line is now authorised.
checklist.done: the evidence pack is filed under the correct retention label and the continuation, deposit and corporate-amendment triggers are live in the calendar.

testing.step: Build the population of business actually bound in the quarter by state and line
actions: Extract every new-business and renewal policy with a bind date inside the quarter, carrying writing company, NAIC company code, state of risk, line of business, policy number, bind date, effective date and written premium.
Include endorsements that add a new state of risk or a new coverage line to an existing policy, because those create the same authorisation question.
Distinct-count the state/line/writing-company combinations present in the quarter — that combination list, not the policy list, is the real test population.
Have the extractor sign the extract with the query, the run date and the row count.
testing.done: a signed extract exists and the distinct state/line/writing-company combination list is fixed.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the premium ledger before sampling
actions: Total the extract's written premium by state and line and compare it to the written premium by state and line in the general ledger for the same quarter.
Investigate any difference above 0.5% of the state total and resolve it as a timing, cancellation or mapping difference before proceeding.
Tie the state totals to the states shown in Schedule T of the most recent statutory statement to catch states carrying premium that the extract missed.
Document the reconciliation with both sets of totals and the explanation of every difference.
testing.done: extract premium ties to the ledger and to Schedule T states, with every difference explained in the workpaper.

testing.step: Rebuild the authorised state/line matrix independently from regulator sources
actions: Without opening the internal CoA register, build a matrix from source: for each writing company pull the state licensing record from NAIC iSite+ and the state's own company search page.
Record for each state the CoA status, effective date, and the lines of authority in the state's wording.
Compare the rebuilt matrix to the internal CoA register and list every difference in status, date or line wording.
Treat every difference as a finding at this stage — the register being wrong is itself a control failure even where no business was written.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt matrix exists and every difference against the internal register is listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of state/line combinations first written during the quarter and 100% of combinations added to the CoA register during the quarter.
Take 25 further policies at random from the remaining population using a seeded random draw, minimum 40 items overall.
Bias the judgemental portion toward surplus-lines-adjacent lines, new writing companies and states entered in the last 12 months.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selection rule so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every newly written and newly authorised combination.

testing.step: Re-perform the coverage call for each sampled state and line
actions: For each sampled item, look the writing company up in the state's own licensing record and read the lines of authority as at the bind date.
Map the policy's product and coverage to the statutory kind of insurance yourself before looking at the internal mapping.
Where the product maps to a kind of insurance not named on the certificate, record an exception even if a broader line appears to encompass it.
Screenshot the state record you relied on into the workpaper with the date of capture.
testing.done: each sampled item carries an independent coverage conclusion and a captured state source page.

testing.step: Trace each authorised combination to the certificate and its identifiers
actions: Open the CoA certificate image for each sampled state and read the CoA number, the issuing state, the company legal name and the NAIC company code from the face of the certificate.
Confirm the legal name and NAIC code on the certificate are the same entity that appears as writing company on the sampled policy — a group affiliate's certificate does not cover a sister company.
Confirm the certificate is the current one and not a superseded edition replaced by a Corporate Amendments filing.
Log any policy written by an entity whose certificate cannot be produced as an automatic fail.
testing.done: every sampled policy traces to a produced certificate for the same legal entity and NAIC code.

testing.step: Test the UCAA filings behind combinations added during the period
actions: For each state/line added in the quarter, open the UCAA submission package and confirm the application type used (Expansion, Primary or Corporate Amendments) was the right one for the change made.
Confirm the Uniform Consent to Service of Process was executed by an officer with board authority and that the biographical affidavits were dated within 12 months of submission.
Confirm every deficiency letter has a dated response filed on or before the state's due date.
Where a corporate change (name, merger, redomestication, change of control) took effect in the quarter, confirm a Corporate Amendments filing was approved before the change was effected, not after.
testing.done: each added combination is supported by the correct application type, valid signatory authority, fresh affidavits and on-time deficiency responses.

testing.step: Recompute the pre-write timing and the deposit and continuation currency
actions: For every sampled item compute bind date minus CoA effective date; a negative number is a use-before-authorisation breach, not a documentation exception.
For each sampled state recompute the deposit held against the state's stated minimum from the custodian certificate and the state requirement sheet.
Confirm the annual continuation fee was paid and the CoA remained in force across the whole quarter, with no lapse day inside the period.
Where a lapse day exists, quantify the policies bound on that day and the premium at risk.
testing.done: no sampled policy was bound before its CoA effective date, deposits meet the state minimum, and any lapse day is quantified.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and exposure
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying state, writing company, line, policy count, written premium and the date range of the exposure.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list — register not updated, product mapped to the wrong statutory line, state switch released early, corporate change not filed, affiliate certificate assumed to cover — and name an owner.
For use-before-authorisation breaches, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and record the decision and its rationale whichever way it goes.
Set the remediation date and carry every open item into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, quantified exposure and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude the test, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold for unauthorised state/line writing.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the evidence references that support it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who prepared no sampled UCAA filing, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Take in the onboarding request and capture the identifiers needed to verify
actions: Receive the onboarding request from the Agency Relations Manager and open a producer onboarding record.
Capture the National Producer Number (NPN), full legal name, resident state, date of birth or FEIN, and for an agency the entity NPN and the names of its designated responsible licensed producers.

Capture the intended selling states and the products the producer will sell, and translate those products into the lines of authority they require (e.g. Life, Accident and Health, Property, Casualty).
Reject the request back to the Agency Relations Manager if no NPN is supplied — do not search on name alone, because names collide and the wrong record ends up verified.
Set the record status to 'Awaiting licence verification' with quoting access explicitly denied.
checklist.done: the record holds a verified NPN, the selling states and the required lines of authority, with access denied by default.

checklist.step: Pull the Producer Database report from NIPR and file it dated
actions: Log in to NIPR and open PDB Reports; run a PDB report on the NPN, selecting all states rather than Connecticut alone.

Read the report sections in order: demographic information, state licence summary, lines of authority, appointments, and the Regulatory Information Retrieval System (RIRS) and Administrative Actions sections.
Save the report as PDF named <NPN>-pdb-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf into the onboarding folder — this dated pull, not a screenshot of a search box, is the verification evidence.
Record the pull date and the reviewer's name on the onboarding record.
checklist.done: a dated full-state PDB report PDF is filed against the producer record with the reviewer named.

checklist.step: Verify licence status, class and expiry for Connecticut and every selling state
actions: For Connecticut, read the licence status field and accept only 'Active'; treat Inactive, Expired, Suspended, Revoked, Surrendered or Pending as a stop.
Read the licence class (resident vs non-resident, producer vs adjuster vs public adjuster) and confirm it is a producer licence for the states where the producer will sell.
Read the original issue date and the expiry date and record both; flag any licence expiring within 60 days for immediate renewal chasing before contracting.
Where the resident state licence is not active, stop — a non-resident licence in Connecticut depends on the resident licence and falls with it.
Write ACTIVE/NOT ACTIVE per state onto the onboarding record with the expiry date.
checklist.done: every selling state shows an active producer licence with a recorded expiry date, or the onboarding is stopped.

checklist.step: Match lines of authority to the products the producer will actually sell
actions: List the products in the proposed appointment and map each to the line of authority Connecticut requires for it, using the CID licensing line definitions rather than internal product naming.
Compare that required list to the lines held on the PDB report for each state and mark each product SELLABLE or NOT SELLABLE.
Where a product needs a line the producer does not hold, either remove the product from the contract scope or require the producer to add the line before contracting.
For variable products confirm the FINRA registration and the state variable line are both present, since the state licence alone is insufficient.
Record the approved product scope on the producer record so downstream systems can enforce it.
checklist.done: each contracted product is matched to a held line of authority, and products without a matching line are removed from scope.

checklist.step: Verify the agency licence and its designated responsible licensed producer
actions: For an agency, run a separate PDB report on the entity NPN — an individual's licence never covers the agency and vice versa.
Confirm the entity licence is active in Connecticut with the lines the agency's producers will sell, and read the designated responsible licensed producer named on the entity record.
Confirm the named DRLP holds an active individual licence with the same lines, and record their NPN against the agency.
Confirm the agency's registered legal name and FEIN match the counterparty on the producer agreement — a DBA on the contract with a different licensed entity is a break.
Link the individual producer records to the agency record so downstream reconciliation can roll up.
checklist.done: the agency entity licence, its DRLP and the contracting legal name are all verified and linked.

checklist.step: Review regulatory actions and disclosures on the PDB before contracting
actions: Read the RIRS and Administrative Actions sections of the PDB report and list every action with its state, date, reason code and disposition.
For each action obtain the underlying consent order or state document and read what actually happened rather than the code alone.
Refer any action involving dishonesty, fraud, misappropriation of premium or a felony to Regulatory Counsel, because it also raises an 18 U.S.C. 1033 question handled under the screening obligation.
Record an accept / accept-with-conditions / decline decision with the reasoning and the reviewer's name.
File the consent orders and the decision in the onboarding folder.
checklist.done: every PDB regulatory action has been read at source and carries a named, reasoned onboarding decision.

checklist.step: Execute the producer agreement only after verification clears
actions: Confirm the onboarding record shows 'Licence verified' before releasing the agreement for signature — the contract is what starts Connecticut's 15-day appointment clock, so it must not precede verification.
Issue the producer agreement with the approved product and state schedule attached, and the commission schedule matched to that scope.
Route through DocuSign and capture the completion certificate showing the execution date and signatories.
Write the executed contract date onto the producer record, because that date drives the appointment deadline calculation.
Store the executed agreement in the producer file.
checklist.done: an executed agreement exists with a captured execution date, and it post-dates the licence verification.

checklist.step: Confirm the appointing entity is the Connecticut-licensed writing company
actions: Open the CoA register and read which group writing companies hold an in-force Connecticut certificate of authority and for which lines.

Confirm the entity that will appoint the producer is one of those companies and that it holds the line the producer will sell — a producer cannot be appointed by an entity not authorised for that line.
Where business will be written across several group companies, list every company that must appoint the producer separately.
Record the appointing company list and NAIC company codes on the producer record.
checklist.done: each appointing company is confirmed as Connecticut-authorised for the relevant line and is recorded with its NAIC code.

checklist.step: Hold quoting, portal and application access until the gate is satisfied
actions: Keep the producer's portal account in 'provisioned, access denied' state so no quote or application can be started before licensing clears.
Configure the portal entitlement to grant only the states and lines on the approved product scope, so a licensed producer cannot stray into an unlicensed line.
Confirm the underwriting workstation and the agency portal both refuse submissions carrying an unverified producer code.
Test the block with one deliberately unverified producer code before go-live and record the result.
Release access only on an automated signal from the producer record, never on an email request.
checklist.done: access is entitlement-scoped to verified states and lines, and the block on unverified codes is demonstrably working.

checklist.step: File the appointment transaction through NIPR within the statutory window
actions: Compute the deadline as the executed-contract date (or the first application date if earlier) plus 15 days, and diarise it.
In NIPR Gateway open the Appointments transaction, select Connecticut and the appointing company by NAIC code, and enter the producer NPN and the lines of authority being appointed.
Submit and pay the state appointment fee, then capture the NIPR transaction confirmation with its reference number and submission date.
Where Connecticut business is written through more than one group company, file a separate appointment per company.
Write the transaction reference and submission date onto the producer record.
checklist.done: an appointment transaction is submitted and confirmed for every appointing company inside the 15-day window.

checklist.step: Confirm the state accepted the appointment and resolve rejections
actions: Re-pull the PDB report 3 to 5 business days after submission and read the appointments section for the Connecticut appointment with the correct company and effective date.
Where the state rejected the transaction, read the rejection reason (licence not active, line not held, fee unpaid, duplicate) and correct and resubmit the same day.
Where the rejection cannot be cured, suspend the producer's access immediately rather than leaving a contracted producer live without an appointment.
File the confirming PDB pull as the appointment evidence and record the state-recorded effective date.
checklist.done: the state's own record shows the appointment active with an effective date, or access is suspended pending cure.

checklist.step: Synchronise licence and appointment data into the operational systems
actions: Load NPN, licence numbers, lines of authority, licence expiry dates, appointment company and appointment effective date onto the producer master record.
Push the same identifiers into the commission platform and the policy administration producer table so all three systems key on NPN and not on a local producer code.
Run a key-integrity check that every active producer code resolves to exactly one NPN and no NPN carries two conflicting statuses.
Fix or quarantine any record failing the check before it can be used on a new application.
Record the load date and the row counts.
checklist.done: NPN-keyed licence and appointment data is consistent across producer, commission and policy systems with a clean key-integrity run.

checklist.step: Arm the commission-hold and application-block rules
actions: Configure the commission rule to hold payment where the producer's licence status is not Active or the appointment for the writing company and state is missing on the policy effective date.
Configure the policy administration submission rule to refuse any application whose producer code fails the same test at the point of application.
Test both rules with a controlled unlicensed producer code and a controlled unappointed producer code and record the outcomes.
Route held commissions to the Producer Compliance Manager for disposition rather than releasing them on a supervisor override.
checklist.done: commission holds and application blocks are configured and demonstrated to fire on both unlicensed and unappointed test cases.

checklist.step: Subscribe to ongoing licence-change alerts from the state records
actions: Enrol every contracted producer in the NIPR PDB alert service so any licence expiry, cancellation, suspension, revocation or line-of-authority change is pushed daily.
Route alerts into the licensing work queue with an SLA of one business day for status-degrading alerts.
On a degrading alert, suspend portal access and set the commission hold before contacting the producer.
Reconcile the alert enrolment list against the contracted roster monthly so new producers are never left unmonitored.
checklist.done: every contracted producer is enrolled in state licence alerts and degrading alerts drive same-day access suspension.

checklist.step: File the verification evidence and attest the onboarding
actions: Move the onboarding folder — dated PDB report, line-of-authority mapping, regulatory-action review, executed agreement, NIPR appointment confirmation and confirming PDB pull — into the compliance evidence repository under Producer Licensing.
Apply the retention label of relationship life plus 5 years after termination.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, producer name, agency and state.
Sign the onboarding attestation recording that the licence was verified before contracting and the appointment was filed within the statutory window.
Close the onboarding record and release access on the system signal.
checklist.done: the evidence pack is filed under the retention label, searchable by NPN, with a signed pre-solicitation attestation.

testing.step: Build the population of producers who actually produced in the quarter
actions: Extract every producer code that appears on an application, a bound policy or a commission payment in the quarter, with NPN, agency, writing company, state and the earliest transaction date in the period.
Join to the policy register so each producer carries the policies and premium attributed to them.
Add producers who only serviced or countersigned, because solicitation is not limited to the writer of record.
Sign the extract with the query, run date and row count.
testing.done: a signed population of producing producers joined to their policies and premium exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the roster to the commission ledger and the policy register
actions: Total commission paid in the quarter by producer from the commission ledger and compare to the producers present in the extract.
List any producer paid commission who does not appear in the roster extract and any roster producer with no payment and no policy.
Trace policy counts by producer from the policy register to the extract and resolve differences before sampling.
Document both totals and every explained difference in the workpaper.
testing.done: the roster ties to commission payments and policy counts, with all differences explained.

testing.step: Re-pull the Producer Database independently for the whole population
actions: Run a bulk PDB report over the population NPNs rather than relying on the internally stored licence fields.
Extract for each NPN the Connecticut licence status, licence class, lines of authority, issue and expiry dates, and every appointment with its company NAIC code and effective date.
Compare the re-pull to the internal producer master field by field and list every difference.
Treat any internal record showing Active where the state shows otherwise as a finding regardless of whether business was written.
testing.done: an independent PDB re-pull exists and every field-level difference against the internal master is listed.

testing.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of producers onboarded during the quarter and 100% of producers flagged by the re-pull as status-mismatched.
Take 25 further producers at random using a seeded draw from the remaining population, minimum 40 items overall.
Weight the judgemental portion toward non-resident producers, agencies with multiple DRLPs and producers writing more than one line.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and rule so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every new and every mismatched producer.

testing.step: Re-perform the pre-solicitation licence test for each sampled producer
actions: For each sampled producer identify the earliest application, quote or bound policy date in the period.
Read the state licence issue date and status history in the PDB and reach your own conclusion on whether an active Connecticut licence existed on that date.
Compare your conclusion to the onboarding record's verification decision before reading the internal reasoning, then note agreement or exception.
Capture the PDB page relied on into the workpaper with the capture date.
testing.done: each sampled producer has an independent pre-solicitation conclusion and a captured state source page.

testing.step: Test the line-of-authority match against what was actually sold
actions: For each sampled producer list the lines actually written from their policies in the quarter.
Compare those lines to the lines of authority the state record shows they held on each policy's application date.
Flag every policy written in a line the producer did not hold, including cases where a broad internal product name masked a distinct statutory line.
Where a variable product was sold, confirm both the state variable line and the FINRA registration were live on the application date.
testing.done: every sampled policy's line is matched to a held line of authority as at its application date, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Trace agency licensing and the designated responsible licensed producer
actions: For sampled agency-sourced business, pull the entity PDB report and confirm the entity licence was active with the written lines on the policy dates.
Confirm the DRLP named on the state record held an active individual licence throughout the period.
Confirm the contracting legal name and FEIN on the producer agreement match the licensed entity, not a DBA or an affiliate.
Log any agency writing under an affiliate's licence as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled agency's entity licence, DRLP and contracting identity are verified against the state record.

testing.step: Recompute the appointment deadline maths and the pre-appointment position
actions: For each sampled producer recompute the deadline as the earlier of the executed contract date and the first application date, plus 15 days.
Compare the recomputed deadline to the NIPR appointment submission date and record the day count over or under.
Confirm the appointing company on the appointment is the same writing company that issued the sampled policies.
Compute the exposure window for any late appointment: the policies and premium written between the deadline and the actual appointment date.
testing.done: every sampled appointment has a recomputed deadline, a measured day count and a quantified exposure where late.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and commission consequence
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception carrying NPN, agency, state, line, policy numbers, premium and commission paid.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list — access released before verification, PDB pull stale, line mapped wrongly, appointment filed late, agency licence assumed from the individual — and name an owner.
Decide and record the commission consequence: clawback, hold release or write-off, with the Commission Analyst executing it.
Refer unlicensed-solicitation cases to Regulatory Counsel for a Connecticut Insurance Department self-report decision and record the outcome either way.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a commission decision and a self-report decision where applicable.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate for unlicensed solicitation and for late appointment separately and compare each to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the evidence behind it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who performed no sampled verification, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with separate exception rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Runs the appointment and termination queue day to day for Alaska and the other 50 jurisdictions; escalates missed windows and for-cause terminations to the Producer Compliance Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska Statutes Title 21, Chapter 27 (licensing of producers and appointment of representatives, including the requirement to notify the Director on appointment and on termination and the for-cause reporting duty) re-read against the current Alaska Division of Insurance producer licensing bulletins each time the procedure is reviewed

In-scope processes.value: Appointment lifecycle events only: new agency contract, first application from an unappointed producer, addition of a line of authority, and every termination — voluntary resignation, non-production cancellation, or for-cause termination for fraud, misappropriation or licence action

In-scope systems.value: NIPR Gateway carries the Appointment and Termination transactions and the Uniform Notice of Termination; the agency/producer management system raises the events and holds the day-count clock

Compliance procedure documented.value: Appointment and Termination Window Procedure — event triggers, day-count rules per state, NIPR transaction steps, termination reason-code selection, for-cause reporting to the Director, and producer notification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Producer Compliance Manager and the Head of Compliance; reviewed annually and on any change to the NAIC Uniform Notice of Termination form or an Alaska bulletin changing the day counts

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven — appointment filed within 15 days of the earlier of the executed agency contract or the first application submitted; termination notice filed with the Director within 30 days of the termination effective date; a copy of the termination notice sent to the producer within 15 days of filing it with the Division

Deadline reminders configured.value: The producer management system opens a countdown on each event: appointment alerts at day 5 and day 10 of 15, termination alerts at day 10 and day 20 of 30, and a breach alert to the Producer Compliance Manager on the final day

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The event record with its trigger date, the NIPR appointment or termination confirmation, the Uniform Notice of Termination, the for-cause supporting file and proof of the copy sent to the producer, retained 5 years from the termination effective date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every appointment or termination filed outside its window is logged with the trigger date, the filing date, the days late, the business written in the gap and the root cause, with the disposition and any Division notification recorded

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late filing remediation and personally approves every for-cause termination report before it goes to the Alaska Division of Insurance

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every appointment-triggering event and every termination event dated in the quarter, taken from the producer management system event log and reconciled to contract executions, first applications and HR/agency separation records

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on the statutory windows — one appointment filed after day 15 or one termination filed after day 30 is a fail; a for-cause termination not reported, or reported as non-cause, is a severe fail escalated to the Head of Compliance immediately

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven, so the day-count exception report runs weekly and the documented test is performed quarterly over all events dated in the quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not sit in Licensing Ops and must not have filed any sampled appointment or termination transaction

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly appointment and termination timeliness workpaper (event population, NIPR re-pull, day-count recomputation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Producer Licensing / Alaska

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Event log with trigger dates, NIPR transaction references and day counts, plus the Uniform Notice of Termination and supporting file for every for-cause case, producible to an Alaska market conduct examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Producer Compliance Manager answers Alaska Division of Insurance appointment and termination inquiries; Regulatory Counsel clears every for-cause narrative before filing, because the statutory immunity depends on the report being made in good faith and without malice

checklist.step: Detect the appointment-triggering event on the day it happens
actions: Subscribe the licensing work queue to three triggers: producer agreement execution completed, first application received from a producer with no active appointment for that writing company and state, and a line of authority added to an existing contract.
On each trigger open an appointment event record carrying producer NPN, appointing company NAIC code, state, lines and the trigger date.
Set the trigger date to the earlier of the contract execution date and the first application date — never the date the queue noticed it.
Confirm with the Agency Relations Manager which date is correct where a contract and an application land in the same week.
Start the 15-day countdown on the event record.
checklist.done: every trigger has an event record with an evidenced trigger date and a running 15-day clock.

checklist.step: Confirm the producer is licensed and the company is authorised before filing
actions: Run a PDB report on the NPN and confirm the Alaska licence is Active with the lines being appointed, because the state rejects appointments against inactive licences and the rejection burns clock.
Check the CoA register that the appointing company holds an in-force Alaska certificate of authority for those lines.
Where either check fails, record the blocker on the event record and escalate the same day rather than letting the clock run silently.
File the dated PDB pull against the event record.
checklist.done: an active Alaska licence and an authorised appointing company are both evidenced before the transaction is attempted.

checklist.step: File the appointment transaction in NIPR Gateway
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the Appointments transaction, select Alaska and the appointing company by NAIC code, and enter the producer NPN and each line of authority being appointed.
Enter the appointment effective date as the trigger date so the state record reflects when the authority actually began.
Submit and pay the Alaska appointment fee, then capture the transaction confirmation with its reference number, submission date and fee amount.
Where several group companies must appoint the same producer, file one transaction per company and record each reference separately.
Write the submission date and reference onto the event record and stop the countdown.
checklist.done: each appointment is submitted with a captured NIPR reference and the countdown is stopped inside 15 days.

checklist.step: Confirm state acceptance and cure rejections without losing the window
actions: Re-pull the PDB 3 to 5 business days after submission and confirm the Alaska appointment appears with the right company and effective date.
Read any rejection reason — licence not active, line not held, fee failure, duplicate appointment — and correct and resubmit the same business day.
Where the rejection cannot be cured inside the 15 days, log a late-filing exception immediately instead of waiting for the eventual acceptance.
File the confirming PDB pull as the appointment evidence.
checklist.done: the state record shows the appointment active, or a late-filing exception is already logged with its reason.

checklist.step: Handle just-in-time appointment states differently from Alaska
actions: Maintain a state matrix marking each jurisdiction as appointment-before-solicitation, appointment-within-a-window (Alaska: 15 days), or just-in-time appointment on first application.
Confirm the matrix state by state against each department's producer licensing page and the NIPR state appointment requirements, and date the check.
Route events to the correct day-count rule automatically from the matrix rather than applying Alaska's 15 days everywhere.
Re-verify the matrix at least annually and immediately on any state bulletin, recording the reviewer and the date.
checklist.done: the state matrix is dated, source-verified, and drives the day count applied to each event.

checklist.step: Detect the termination event and fix its effective date
actions: Subscribe to termination triggers: producer resignation, contract cancellation for non-production, cancellation for cause, agency separation notified by HR or Agency Relations, and licence lapse or revocation reported by the PDB alert feed.
Open a termination event record with the producer NPN, the appointing companies affected, the states and the termination effective date as stated in the cancellation notice.
Where the notice gives no date, obtain a written date from the Agency Relations Manager rather than assuming the notification date.
Start the 30-day countdown for the state notice and the 15-day countdown for the copy to the producer.
checklist.done: every termination has an event record with an evidenced effective date and both countdowns running.

checklist.step: Classify the termination reason before touching NIPR
actions: Classify the termination as not-for-cause (resignation, non-production, business realignment, retirement, death) or for-cause.

Treat as for-cause any termination connected to the statutory reasons — fraud, misappropriation or conversion of premium or funds, forgery, misrepresentation to a customer, licence suspension or revocation, felony conviction, or violation of an insurance law.
Select the NAIC termination reason code that matches the classification and record why that code and not a neighbouring one.
Never soften a for-cause termination into non-production to avoid the report — the misclassification is itself the violation.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the classification on every for-cause case before filing.
checklist.done: each termination has a reason code, a written rationale, and counsel confirmation where it is for-cause.

checklist.step: Assemble the supporting file behind a for-cause termination
actions: Collect the underlying evidence: SIU or investigation report, premium account reconciliation showing the shortfall, customer complaints, the internal interview notes and the termination letter.
Write a factual narrative stating what happened, when, the amounts involved and how it was discovered, with no characterisation beyond what the documents support.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the narrative for good faith and absence of malice, because the statutory immunity for the report depends on it.
Store the file under the producer NPN and link it to the termination event record so it can accompany a Division request for the documents.
checklist.done: a counsel-reviewed factual narrative and its supporting documents are filed and linked to the event.

checklist.step: File the termination notice with the Alaska Director within 30 days
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the Terminations transaction, select Alaska and each affected appointing company by NAIC code, and enter the NPN, the termination effective date and the selected reason code.
For for-cause terminations complete the Uniform Notice of Termination narrative fields with the counsel-approved wording and attach the supporting documents where the transaction permits.
Submit and capture the confirmation with the reference number and submission date, then compute and record days elapsed from the termination effective date.
File a separate termination per appointing company — one filing does not clear appointments held by affiliates.
Stop the 30-day countdown on the event record.
checklist.done: a termination transaction is confirmed for every affected company within 30 days of the effective date.

checklist.step: Send the producer their copy of the notice within 15 days of filing
actions: Generate the producer's copy of the termination notice and any supporting documents filed with the Division.
Send it to the producer's last known address of record by a method that produces proof of dispatch and a delivery record, within 15 days of the filing date.
Include the statutory notice that the producer may file written comments or rebuttal with the Division.
File the proof of dispatch against the event record and record the send date so the 15-day count can be tested.
checklist.done: the producer copy is dispatched with proof, within 15 days of the Division filing, with the rebuttal notice included.

checklist.step: Report material changes to the facts after the original filing
actions: Watch for post-filing developments: investigation conclusions, restitution, criminal charges, or facts that contradict the original narrative.
File an amended or supplemental notice with the Division within 30 days of learning the new facts, referencing the original transaction number.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the supplement on the same good-faith basis as the original.
Record the supplement date and reference on the event record and re-issue the producer copy where the narrative materially changed.
checklist.done: every material post-filing change is reported within 30 days with a referenced supplemental notice.

checklist.step: Cut off access, submissions and commissions on the termination date
actions: Disable the producer's portal and underwriting workstation access effective the termination date so no new submission can be taken.
Set the policy administration producer status to terminated so applications quoting that producer code are refused.
Instruct the Commission Analyst to stop new-business commission and to apply the renewal or vesting treatment the producer agreement provides.
Reassign the in-force book to a licensed and appointed servicing producer and notify affected policyholders where the agreement requires it.
Record the access-revocation timestamp on the event record.
checklist.done: access, submissions and new-business commission are stopped on the termination date and the book is reassigned to an appointed producer.

checklist.step: Work the day-count exception report weekly
actions: Run the weekly report listing every open appointment event past day 10 and every open termination event past day 20, by state and appointing company.
Chase each open item to a named owner with a same-week resolution date.
Escalate anything that will breach its window to the Head of Compliance before the breach, not after.
Record the weekly run, the open counts and the actions taken so the control has a running history.
checklist.done: the weekly report is run, every ageing event has a named owner, and pending breaches are escalated before the deadline.

checklist.step: Reinstate correctly where a terminated producer returns
actions: Treat a returning producer as a fresh onboarding: re-pull the PDB, re-verify the Alaska licence and lines, and re-read the RIRS section for anything added since the termination.
Where the earlier termination was for cause, refer the return to the Producer Compliance Manager and Regulatory Counsel before any contract is issued.
File a new appointment transaction with a new effective date; do not attempt to revive the terminated appointment.
Record the link between the old termination event and the new appointment event so the history stays readable.
checklist.done: returning producers are re-verified and newly appointed, with for-cause histories cleared by counsel first.

checklist.step: File the event evidence and attest the window compliance
actions: Move each closed event folder — trigger evidence, PDB pulls, NIPR confirmations, Uniform Notice of Termination, for-cause file and proof of the producer copy — into the compliance evidence repository under Producer Licensing / Appointments and Terminations.
Apply the 5-year-from-termination retention label.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, appointing company NAIC code, state and event date.
Sign the monthly attestation stating that all appointment and termination events closed in the month met their statutory windows, listing any that did not.
checklist.done: event evidence is filed under the retention label and a signed monthly window-compliance attestation exists, exceptions listed.

testing.step: Build the population of appointment and termination events in the quarter
actions: Extract every appointment and termination event with a trigger or effective date inside the quarter, carrying NPN, appointing company NAIC code, state, event type, trigger date and filing date.
Separately extract the underlying source events — executed producer agreements, first applications from unappointed producers, and agency separations — so events the queue never opened can be found.
Sign the extract with the query, run date and row counts for each event type.
testing.done: a signed population of events plus an independent extract of underlying source events exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the event population to the source of record for completeness
actions: Match every executed producer agreement in the quarter to an appointment event; list agreements with no event.
Match every first application from a producer with no prior appointment to an appointment event; list unmatched applications.
Match every agency separation and HR termination record to a termination event; list unmatched separations.
Treat every unmatched source record as a completeness exception, since a missing event never gets a day count at all.
testing.done: every contract, first application and separation ties to an event, or is listed as a completeness exception.

testing.step: Re-pull the state appointment record independently
actions: Run a bulk PDB report over the population NPNs and extract every Alaska appointment with company NAIC code, effective date and termination date.
Compare the state record to the internal event log and list appointments live in the state record that the internal roster shows as terminated, and vice versa.
Confirm each filed termination actually removed the appointment on the state record rather than merely being submitted.
List every difference as a finding before sampling.
testing.done: the state appointment record is reconciled to the internal event log with every difference listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations and 100% of events already flagged as late by the weekly report.
Take 25 further events at random using a seeded draw across both event types, minimum 40 items overall.
Weight the judgemental portion toward events with several appointing companies and toward producers who wrote business close to their trigger date.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and rule.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and includes every for-cause termination and every known late event.

testing.step: Recompute the appointment window from the underlying source documents
actions: For each sampled appointment open the executed agreement and the first application and read both dates yourself rather than accepting the recorded trigger date.
Recompute the deadline as the earlier of those two dates plus 15 days.
Compare to the NIPR submission date and record days early or late; a trigger date recorded later than the source documents support is itself an exception.
Capture the agreement signature page and the application date field into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled appointment has a source-recomputed deadline and a measured day count with captured source evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the termination windows including the producer copy
actions: For each sampled termination read the effective date from the cancellation notice or separation record, not from the event field.
Recompute effective date plus 30 days and compare to the NIPR termination submission date.
Recompute filing date plus 15 days and compare to the proof-of-dispatch date on the producer's copy.
Record both day counts and treat a missing proof of dispatch as a fail on the producer-notice leg even where the state filing was timely.
testing.done: both the 30-day state leg and the 15-day producer leg are recomputed and evidenced for every sampled termination.

testing.step: Re-perform the for-cause classification independently
actions: Read the underlying investigation file for each sampled termination, including those coded non-production, before looking at the assigned reason code.
Reach your own for-cause or not-for-cause conclusion against the statutory grounds — fraud, misappropriation of premium, forgery, misrepresentation, licence action, felony, insurance law violation.
Compare to the code filed; a for-cause fact pattern filed as non-production is a severe exception, reported immediately rather than at the end of the test.
Confirm the filed narrative is factual, supported by the documents and cleared by counsel before filing.
testing.done: each sampled termination carries an independent classification conclusion and a supported, counsel-cleared narrative.

testing.step: Test whether business was written in the appointment gap
actions: For every late appointment, list the applications and bound policies attributed to that producer between the trigger date and the state-recorded appointment effective date.
For every late or missing termination, list submissions taken after the termination effective date to prove the access cut-off held.
Quantify the policy count, premium and commission in each gap.
Trace one policy per gap end to end to confirm the exposure is real and not a data artefact.
testing.done: the business written inside each gap is quantified and at least one policy per gap is traced end to end.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and regulatory consequence
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with NPN, appointing company, state, event type, trigger date, filing date, days late and gap exposure.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list — trigger not detected, wrong trigger date used, NIPR rejection not cured, affiliate company missed, reason code softened, producer copy not sent — and name an owner.
Refer misclassified for-cause terminations and unreported terminations to Regulatory Counsel for an Alaska Division of Insurance notification decision and record the outcome.
Set remediation dates and carry every open item into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, quantified exposure and a notification decision where relevant.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute three exception rates separately: late appointments, late terminations, and misclassified or unreported for-cause terminations.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the evidence behind each rate.
Have the Internal Auditor, who filed none of the sampled transactions, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting, flagging every for-cause finding separately, and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with three stated exception rates, a conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the renewal calendar for producer licences, appointment renewals and the company's Alaska certificate of authority continuation; escalates lapse risk to the Producer Compliance Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska Statutes Title 21, Chapter 27 for producer licence renewal and continuing education (24 CE hours per biennial period including 3 hours of ethics) and Title 21, Chapter 09 for the insurer's annual certificate of authority continuation, checked against the current Alaska Division of Insurance renewal bulletins and CE requirement sheet each cycle

In-scope processes.value: Renewal cycle management: producer licence renewals by state cycle, CE assignment and credit banking, annual appointment renewal invoices, entity licence renewals, and the insurer's annual certificate of authority continuation and annual statement filing

In-scope systems.value: NIPR Gateway for renewal transactions and the PDB for the authoritative expiry dates and CE transcript position; the learning management system delivers and evidences CE, and the licensing register carries the CoA continuation dates

Compliance procedure documented.value: Licence Renewal and CE Procedure — calendar build from PDB expiry dates, T-120/90/60/30 notice cadence, CE curriculum assignment and credit reconciliation, carrier-paid renewal handling, lapse and reinstatement rules, and the annual CoA continuation checklist

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Producer Compliance Manager and the Head of Compliance; reviewed each renewal cycle and on any Alaska change to CE hours, ethics hours or the renewal cadence

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Alaska producer licences renew on a biennial cycle with CE completed before the licence expiry date; appointment renewals are billed annually by the Division; the insurer's certificate of authority continues annually on payment of the continuation fee alongside the March 1 annual statement filing

Deadline reminders configured.value: Renewal calendar alerts at T-120, T-90, T-60 and T-30 days to each producer licence expiry, a separate CE-shortfall alert at T-90 for any producer under the required hours, and a January alert for the March 1 annual statement and CoA continuation payment

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Renewal calendar snapshot, PDB transcript pulls, LMS CE completion certificates, NIPR renewal confirmations, appointment renewal invoices and receipts, and the CoA continuation receipt, retained 5 years from the end of the renewal cycle

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every lapsed producer licence, CE shortfall at expiry, unpaid appointment renewal and any late CoA continuation is logged with the lapse dates, business written while lapsed and the reinstatement path taken
