checklist.step: Build the renewal calendar from the state record, not the internal fields
actions: Run a bulk PDB report across every contracted producer NPN and extract, per state, the licence expiry date, the licence class and the lines held.
Load those expiry dates into the renewal calendar as the authoritative dates, overwriting any internally keyed value.
Group producers into renewal cohorts by month of expiry so the workload is visible a quarter ahead.
Reconcile the calendar row count to the contracted roster count and investigate any producer with no expiry date returned.
Date and file the bulk PDB extract as the calendar's source evidence.
checklist.done: the calendar is built from a dated PDB extract, covers every contracted producer and reconciles to the roster count.

checklist.step: Determine each state's CE requirement for the cycle
actions: For Alaska read the Division of Insurance CE requirement sheet and record the hours required per biennial cycle (24 hours) and the ethics component (3 hours).
Record line-specific requirements such as annuity suitability training, long-term care training and flood (NFIP) training where the producer sells those products.
Record the carry-over rule, the approved-provider rule and whether self-study or classroom limits apply.
Build the same record for every state a contracted producer holds a licence in, because non-resident producers usually satisfy CE through the resident state.
Date the requirement record and name the reviewer so the basis for the assignment is auditable.
checklist.done: a dated, per-state CE requirement record exists covering hours, ethics, line-specific training and carry-over rules.

checklist.step: Assign the CE curriculum early in the cycle
actions: Build a curriculum per state and per line combination that meets the hours and the ethics component from state-approved course providers only.
Assign the curriculum to each producer at the start of the cycle with an internal completion target of 90 days before licence expiry, not the expiry date itself.
Configure the LMS to record provider name, course number, approved credit hours, ethics flag and completion date for every course.
Publish a producer-facing progress view so each producer can see hours banked against hours required.
Send the first completion reminder at cycle start rather than waiting for the shortfall report.
checklist.done: every producer has a state-approved curriculum assigned with an internal target 90 days ahead of expiry and a visible progress view.

checklist.step: Reconcile CE credits banked at the state against the LMS
actions: Pull the state CE transcript position for each producer from the PDB CE section and compare hours banked to the LMS completion record.
Investigate every difference — the usual causes are a provider failing to report credits to the state, a course taken outside the approved provider list, or credits posted to a different state.
Chase the provider directly for unreported credits and record the chase date and the provider contact.
Never treat an LMS completion as satisfying the requirement — only the credit banked at the state counts.
Record the reconciled hours and ethics hours on the producer record with the transcript pull date.
checklist.done: state-banked hours reconcile to the LMS for every producer, with unreported credits chased and dated.

checklist.step: Run the CE shortfall report and chase before it becomes a lapse
actions: Run the shortfall report at T-120 and T-90 days to expiry listing producers below required hours, below the ethics component, or missing a line-specific training.
Send each named producer their gap in hours and course numbers, copied to their Agency Relations Manager, with a completion date 60 days before expiry.
Escalate any producer still short at T-30 to the Head of Distribution with the production volume at risk so the business consequence is visible.
Record every chase and escalation against the producer record.
checklist.done: every shortfall producer has a dated chase with a named gap and an escalation on record if still short at T-30.

checklist.step: Confirm who pays and file the renewal transaction
actions: Read the producer agreement to confirm whether the renewal fee is carrier-paid or producer-paid and record it on the producer record, since carrier-paid renewals are the company's obligation to complete.
For carrier-paid producers open the NIPR licence renewal transaction, confirm the CE requirement is satisfied on the state record, submit and pay the Alaska renewal fee.
Capture the NIPR confirmation with reference number, submission date and fee amount against the producer record.
For producer-paid renewals send the renewal instruction and then verify completion on the PDB rather than accepting the producer's word.
Record renewal complete only when the PDB shows a new expiry date.
checklist.done: each renewal shows a new state-recorded expiry date, with the payer identified and the confirmation filed.

checklist.step: Renew entity licences and confirm the designated responsible licensed producer
actions: Run the renewal calendar for entity NPNs separately, because agency licence cycles rarely align with the individual cycles.
Before renewing, confirm the designated responsible licensed producer named on the entity record still holds an active individual licence and is still with the agency.
Where the DRLP has left, file the DRLP change transaction before the renewal so the entity does not renew with a stale responsible producer.
Confirm the entity's legal name, address of record and FEIN are current, and file the change transaction where they are not.
Capture the renewal confirmation and the new entity expiry date.
checklist.done: each entity licence is renewed with a verified, current DRLP and current entity details on the state record.

checklist.step: Reconcile and pay the annual appointment renewal invoice
actions: Retrieve the Alaska appointment renewal invoice for each appointing company when the Division issues it and export the appointed-producer list it bills for.
Reconcile the billed list to the internal contracted roster line by line before paying, so terminated producers are not renewed and paid for.
File the outstanding termination transactions for anyone on the invoice who should already have been terminated, and note the fee that was avoided or wasted.
Pay the reconciled invoice before the Division's due date and capture the receipt and payment date.
Re-pull the PDB after payment and confirm the appointments continued rather than cancelling for non-payment.
checklist.done: the invoice is reconciled to the roster, paid on time, and the state record shows the appointments continued.

checklist.step: Handle lapses immediately when a licence expires unrenewed
actions: On the PDB alert or the day-after-expiry report, suspend the producer's portal access and set the commission hold the same day.
Set the policy administration producer status so no new application can be taken under that producer code.
Quantify immediately whether any application or bind occurred after the expiry date and, if so, open an unlicensed-production exception.
Notify the producer and their Agency Relations Manager in writing that they may not solicit until the licence is reinstated.
Reassign urgent servicing work to a licensed and appointed producer.
checklist.done: access and commissions are stopped on the expiry date and any post-expiry production is quantified the same day.

checklist.step: Work the reinstatement path within the state's window
actions: Read Alaska's reinstatement rules: the period in which a lapsed licence may be reinstated on payment of the renewal fee plus a penalty, and the point beyond which a new application and re-examination are required.
Compute the reinstatement deadline from the expiry date and diarise it with a T-30 alert.
Confirm the CE deficiency that caused the lapse is cured and banked at the state before submitting the reinstatement.
Submit the reinstatement or new application transaction and capture the confirmation and the new expiry date.
Re-file the appointment where the lapse cancelled it, because reinstating the licence does not automatically restore the appointment.
checklist.done: the reinstatement is filed inside the state window with CE cured, and the appointment is re-filed where it was cancelled.

checklist.step: Continue the company's Alaska certificate of authority for the year
actions: Open the CoA register for each writing company holding an Alaska certificate and read the continuation date and fee basis.
Confirm the annual statement and supporting statutory filings will be filed by the March 1 due date, because continuation is conditioned on the company remaining in good standing.
Raise and pay the continuation fee, including any retaliatory element, ahead of the due date and capture the receipt.
Re-verify the statutory deposit still meets the Alaska requirement and record the custodian certificate date.
Update the register with the new continuation date and confirm the company shows as active on the Division's company search.
checklist.done: the continuation fee is paid on time, the deposit is re-verified and the Division's record shows the company active for the new year.

checklist.step: Refresh the roster for corporate changes that invalidate renewals
actions: Check whether any writing company changed name, merged, redomesticated or changed lines during the cycle, since each requires a UCAA Corporate Amendments filing and can change the appointing entity on every appointment.
Where a change occurred, confirm the Corporate Amendments filing was approved and then confirm the appointments were re-filed under the surviving NAIC company code.
Update the producer records and the appointment renewal invoice expectations for the new company structure.
Record the change reference and the date the appointments were re-pointed.
checklist.done: every corporate change in the cycle has an approved amendment and appointments re-pointed to the surviving company code.

checklist.step: Report renewal health to Distribution and Compliance monthly
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard showing renewals due in the next 120 days, CE shortfall counts, lapses in the month, reinstatements outstanding and appointment renewal payment status.
Show production at risk in written premium next to each shortfall cohort so Distribution can act on the number that matters to them.
Walk the Head of Distribution and the Head of Compliance through the exceptions and record the agreed actions and owners.
Carry unresolved actions forward month to month rather than resetting the dashboard.
checklist.done: a monthly dashboard is published with production at risk, walked through with Distribution and Compliance, and actions carried forward.

checklist.step: Bank the evidence for every renewal and CE cycle
actions: File per producer: the dated PDB expiry extract, CE transcript pull, LMS completion certificates with provider and course numbers, the NIPR renewal confirmation and the new expiry date.
File per company: the appointment renewal invoice, the reconciliation, the payment receipt and the CoA continuation receipt.
Apply the 5-year-from-cycle-end retention label and confirm records are searchable by NPN, state, cycle and company NAIC code.
Snapshot the renewal calendar at cycle end so the population can be rebuilt exactly as it stood.
checklist.done: renewal and CE evidence is filed under the retention label with a cycle-end calendar snapshot preserved.

checklist.step: Attest the cycle and close it
actions: Confirm every producer in the cycle is either renewed with a new state expiry date, lapsed with access removed, or terminated.
Confirm every CE requirement including the ethics component was banked at the state before expiry, listing any that were not.
Confirm every appointment renewal invoice and CoA continuation for the period is paid with a receipt on file.
Sign the cycle attestation naming the exceptions and their tracker references and route it to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: a signed cycle attestation exists showing every producer's end state and every unpaid or short item listed with a tracker reference.

testing.step: Build the population of renewals and CE cycles falling due
actions: Extract every contracted producer and entity whose licence expiry date, CE cycle end or appointment renewal fell inside the quarter, with NPN, state, expiry date and cycle dates.
Add every writing company whose Alaska certificate of authority continuation fell due in the period.
Sign the extract with the query, run date and row count.
testing.done: a signed population of due renewals, CE cycles and CoA continuations exists.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the state record for completeness
actions: Run an independent bulk PDB extract over the whole contracted roster and list every licence with an expiry date inside the quarter.
Compare that list to the internal population and list producers the internal calendar missed entirely.
Confirm the entity NPNs were extracted as well as the individuals, since agency cycles are the usual omission.
Treat every producer missing from the internal calendar as a completeness exception before any sampling.
testing.done: the internal renewal calendar is reconciled to the state record with every omission listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of producers who lapsed in the quarter and 100% of CoA continuations due.
Take 25 further producers at random using a seeded draw across renewed and reinstated producers, minimum 40 items overall.
Weight the judgemental portion toward carrier-paid renewals, multi-state producers and producers who sold annuity or long-term care products with extra training requirements.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and rule.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and includes every lapse and every CoA continuation in the period.

testing.step: Re-perform the renewal outcome against the state record
actions: For each sampled producer pull the PDB and read the current licence status and the new expiry date.
Confirm the new expiry date is consistent with a completed renewal and not simply an internally updated field.
Compare the renewal transaction date to the old expiry date and record any renewal completed after expiry as a lapse regardless of how quickly it was cured.
Capture the PDB page into the workpaper with the capture date.
testing.done: each sampled renewal is confirmed against the state record with the transaction date compared to the old expiry.

testing.step: Recompute the CE hours banked including the ethics component
actions: For each sampled producer read the state CE transcript and total the credit hours banked in the cycle and the hours flagged as ethics.
Compare to the Alaska requirement of 24 hours including 3 ethics hours for the biennial cycle, and to the line-specific training requirements for the products they sold.
Confirm the credits were banked before the licence expiry date, not after, and that every course came from a state-approved provider.
Treat LMS completions with no corresponding state-banked credit as a shortfall, not a reporting delay, unless the provider chase is evidenced and dated before expiry.
testing.done: recomputed state-banked hours meet the requirement including ethics and line-specific training, banked before expiry.

testing.step: Test the appointment renewal invoice reconciliation and payment
actions: Take the Alaska appointment renewal invoice for the period and re-perform the reconciliation against the contracted roster as it stood at the invoice date.
List producers billed and paid for who were already terminated internally, and quantify the wasted fee and the period they remained appointed at the state.
List producers on the roster who were not on the invoice, since those appointments may already have cancelled.
Trace the payment to the receipt and to the ledger and confirm it landed before the Division's due date.
testing.done: the invoice reconciliation is re-performed, zombie appointments are quantified and the payment is traced as on time.

testing.step: Test the certificate of authority continuation for each writing company
actions: For each Alaska-licensed writing company confirm the annual statement was filed by March 1 and the continuation fee was paid before its due date, from the receipt not the register field.
Confirm the statutory deposit certificate is current and still meets the Alaska requirement.
Confirm the Division's company search shows the company active with the same lines for the new year.
Log any day on which the certificate was not in force and quantify the business bound on that day.
testing.done: each company's continuation is evidenced from receipts and the state record, with any non-force day quantified.

testing.step: Quantify business written during any lapse window
actions: For every lapsed producer list applications, bound policies and commission paid between the expiry date and the reinstatement date.
Confirm the portal access suspension timestamp is on or before the expiry date, and flag any gap between expiry and suspension.
Confirm the commission hold fired and that no supervisor override released payment during the lapse.
Trace one policy per lapse window end to end to prove the exposure is real.
testing.done: every lapse window has quantified production, a checked access-suspension timestamp and one traced policy.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with NPN or company code, state, cycle dates, the shortfall or lapse length and the production or fee exposure.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list — calendar built from internal dates, CE credits never banked at the state, carrier-paid renewal missed, entity cycle overlooked, invoice paid without reconciliation, continuation fee late — and name an owner.
Record the remediation: reinstatement filed, CE cured, fee recovered, or self-report decision cleared by Regulatory Counsel for production on a lapsed licence.
Carry every open item into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, quantified exposure and a recorded remediation.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute separate rates for lapsed licences, CE shortfalls at expiry, unreconciled appointment renewals and late CoA continuations.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the evidence behind each rate.
Have the Internal Auditor, who processed no sampled renewal or CE posting, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with four stated rates, a conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 18 U.S.C. 1033(e)(1) (prohibition on a person convicted of a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust engaging in the business of insurance) and 1033(e)(2) (written consent of the appropriate state insurance regulator), read with Alaska Statutes Title 21, Chapter 27 on licensing character and fitness and the Division's 1033 written-consent instructions, re-read at each procedure review

In-scope processes.value: Pre-engagement screening at every entry point into the business of insurance: employee hire and internal transfer into an insurance function, producer and agency onboarding, and contractor or vendor staff placed in underwriting, claims, premium handling or policyholder-facing roles

In-scope systems.value: Applicant tracking carries the 1033 attestation and the FCRA disclosure and authorisation; consumer report results are ordered through the background vendor, adjudication decisions are stored in HRIS and the producer-side screen is driven from the NIPR PDB regulatory-action sections

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per hire and per producer engagement — the screen must clear before the start date or the first solicitation; where a conviction is disclosed, the FCRA pre-adverse action notice must be sent with a copy of the report and the summary of rights and a minimum of 5 business days allowed before the adverse action notice; the 1033 written-consent application is filed before any engagement, not after

Deadline reminders configured.value: Applicant tracking blocks a start date until the screen is cleared and alerts the recruiter at T-10 and T-3 business days; the FCRA pre-adverse clock is diarised on send with an alert on the fifth business day; open written-consent applications are chased every 30 days until the Division responds

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed attestation, FCRA disclosure and authorisation, the consumer report, certified court dispositions, the adjudication record with its reasoning, the 1033 written-consent application and the Division's consent letter, retained 7 years after the engagement ends in a restricted-access store

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any person engaged in the business of insurance without a completed screen, and any prohibited person engaged without a written consent, is logged with the engagement dates, the role and the duties performed, plus the removal and notification decision

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every decision to engage or retain a person with a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust, and every remediation where a prohibited person was engaged without consent

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every hire, internal transfer into an insurance function, producer onboarding and contractor placement with a start date inside the quarter, taken from HRIS, the applicant tracking system, the producer management system and the contingent-worker register

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — one person engaged in the business of insurance without a completed pre-engagement screen is a fail, and any prohibited person engaged without a written 1033 consent on file is a severe fail escalated to the General Counsel on discovery

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation fires per hire and per engagement, so the screen-completion exception report runs weekly and the documented test is performed quarterly over that quarter's starters, with an annual 100% re-attestation sweep of the existing population

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly 1033 screening workpaper (starter population, screen completion reconciliation, adjudication re-performance, consent tracking, exception log) in the restricted section of the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Screening register with person, role, engagement date, screen completion date, adjudication outcome and consent letter reference, producible to the Alaska Division of Insurance or a market conduct examiner within 5 business days without exposing the underlying consumer reports

Regulator response path.value: The Compliance Officer answers Division 1033 consent correspondence; Employment Counsel handles candidate and employee disputes over adverse action and the General Counsel is notified before any admission that a prohibited person was engaged

checklist.step: Define exactly who is in scope for the 1033 screen
actions: Write the in-scope population definition: anyone who acts as, or is employed by, or acts on behalf of an insurer and whose activities affect interstate commerce — underwriting, claims, premium handling, policy service, actuarial, distribution, and management over those functions.
Add contractors and vendor staff who perform those duties, because the prohibition follows the activity and not the payroll.
Name the small set of genuinely out-of-scope roles (for example facilities or catering staff with no insurance duties) and record why each is out.
Have Employment Counsel and the Chief HR Officer confirm the definition in writing.
Publish the definition to Talent Acquisition, HR Business Partners, Procurement and Agency Relations so every entry point applies the same test.
checklist.done: a counsel-confirmed, published in-scope definition exists with the out-of-scope roles named and justified.

checklist.step: Put the 1033 attestation into every application and contract
actions: Add a required attestation question to the application asking whether the person has been convicted of any felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust, or any felony under 18 U.S.C. 1033.

Word it to the statutory standard rather than a general criminal-history question, and state that a yes answer does not automatically disqualify but requires a written consent from the state insurance regulator.
Mirror the same attestation into the producer agreement and the vendor staffing agreement, with a duty to notify within 5 business days of any subsequent conviction.
Configure the applicant tracking workflow so a yes answer routes automatically to Compliance rather than to the hiring manager.
Record the attestation response, its date and the version of the wording used.
checklist.done: the statutory-standard attestation is live in applications, producer agreements and vendor contracts, with yes answers auto-routed to Compliance.

checklist.step: Issue the FCRA disclosure and authorisation before ordering anything
actions: Send the standalone written disclosure that a consumer report may be obtained for employment purposes — a separate document, not buried in the application or the offer letter.
Obtain the candidate's written authorisation and store it with a timestamp before any order is placed.
Provide any state-specific notices and the summary of rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act.
Where state or local fair-chance law delays criminal-history inquiry until after a conditional offer, sequence the order accordingly and record the sequencing rule applied.
Block the vendor order in the workflow until the signed authorisation is on file.
checklist.done: a standalone disclosure and a timestamped signed authorisation exist before any consumer report is ordered.

checklist.step: Order the background check to the scope the screen actually needs
actions: Order county, state and federal criminal searches across the residence and employment history for the statutory look-back the vendor applies, plus a national criminal database search and a sex offender registry search.
Add identity verification and employment and education verification so an undisclosed name or gap cannot hide a conviction.
For roles handling premium or claim funds add the credit report where permitted by state law and justified by the role.
Set the vendor to return dispositions and charge levels, because a felony versus misdemeanour distinction and the nature of the offence are what the 1033 test turns on.
Record the order date, scope ordered and vendor reference on the screening record.
checklist.done: the ordered scope covers criminal jurisdictions, identity and history verification and returns charge level and disposition, with the order logged.

checklist.step: Adjudicate each hit against the 1033 test, not a general criminality test
actions: For each reported conviction record the jurisdiction, charge, statute cited, felony or misdemeanour classification, conviction date and disposition.

Apply the two-part test: is it a felony, and does it involve dishonesty or breach of trust (theft, fraud, forgery, embezzlement, false statements, bribery) or is it a felony under 18 U.S.C. 1033 itself.
Classify each as PROHIBITED (felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust), NOT PROHIBITED (no felony, or felony without a dishonesty or breach-of-trust element), or NEEDS DOCUMENTS.
Never classify from the vendor's summary line alone where the charge wording is ambiguous — escalate it instead.
Write the classification, the reasoning and the reviewer's name onto the screening record.
checklist.done: every conviction carries a two-part 1033 classification with written reasoning and a named reviewer.

checklist.step: Obtain the certified court documents for ambiguous or prohibiting records
actions: Request from the candidate, or order from the court of conviction, the certified judgment and sentencing order and the charging document.
Read the statute the person was convicted under and confirm the felony classification and the elements of the offence, rather than relying on the charge name.
Check for expungement, set-aside, pardon or restoration of rights, and record what each does and does not do to the 1033 prohibition.
Have Regulatory Counsel review any record where the dishonesty or breach-of-trust element is arguable and record their conclusion.
File the certified documents in the restricted screening store.
checklist.done: every prohibiting or ambiguous record is supported by certified court documents and a counsel conclusion on the elements.

checklist.step: Hold the engagement while the classification is open
actions: Keep the start date blocked in the applicant tracking and HRIS workflow until the screening record reads CLEARED or CONSENT OBTAINED.
For producers keep the portal access denied and the appointment unfiled while the classification is open.
Refuse verbal or manager-level overrides in writing and record any override request that was made and declined.
Where an existing employee's later conviction comes to light, remove them from insurance duties immediately while the classification runs, rather than after.
checklist.done: no in-scope person can start, solicit or perform insurance duties while their classification is open, and override attempts are recorded.

checklist.step: Run the FCRA pre-adverse action step properly where the report drives the decision
actions: Send the pre-adverse action notice with a copy of the consumer report and the FCRA summary of rights, before any decision is communicated.
Allow a reasonable period, worked as a minimum of 5 business days, for the person to dispute accuracy or provide context, and diarise the date.
Consider anything the person submits, including evidence the record belongs to someone else or was later reduced, and record the consideration.
Where the decision stands, send the adverse action notice naming the consumer reporting agency, stating it did not make the decision, and setting out the right to a free report and to dispute.
Retain both notices with their send dates in the screening record.
checklist.done: pre-adverse and adverse notices are sent in sequence with the dispute window observed and the response considered on record.

checklist.step: Decide and open the 1033 written consent route where the person is prohibited
actions: Confirm with Regulatory Counsel which regulator is the appropriate one to consent — normally the insurance regulator of the state where the person will be engaged or licensed, so Alaska for an Alaska engagement.
Decide with the hiring executive whether the company will sponsor the consent application at all, and record that business decision with its rationale.
Where the answer is no, close the screen with the adverse action already served and record the outcome.
Where the answer is yes, assign an owner and a target filing date and keep the engagement blocked meanwhile.
checklist.done: a documented decision exists on whether to sponsor a written-consent application, with the correct consenting regulator identified.

checklist.step: Prepare and file the written consent application with the Alaska Division
actions: Assemble the Division's 1033 written consent package: the application form, the certified judgment and sentencing order, evidence of completion of sentence, probation and restitution, and a personal statement.
Add the employer letter describing the exact role, the duties, the supervision arrangements and the controls over any access to premium, claim funds or policyholder data.
Add character references and evidence of rehabilitation where the Division's instructions ask for them, and complete any fingerprint requirement the Division imposes.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the package, then file it with the Alaska Division of Insurance and capture the submission date and reference.
Chase the Division every 30 days and record each contact until a written decision is received.
checklist.done: a counsel-reviewed consent package is filed with a captured reference and a 30-day chase log running until the Division responds.

checklist.step: Act on the Division's decision and record its conditions
actions: On a granted consent, read the letter for conditions — role limits, no handling of funds, supervision, duration or reporting obligations — and record each as a control the manager must apply.
Configure the role restrictions in the operating systems (system entitlements, approval limits, no premium handling) so a condition is enforced and not merely promised.
On a denial, remove the person from any insurance duty immediately and complete the adverse action process.
File the consent or denial letter against the person's screening record and set a review date where the consent is time-limited.
Report granted consents with conditions to the Head of Compliance in the monthly pack.
checklist.done: the Division's decision is filed, its conditions are configured as enforced system restrictions, and any expiry is diarised.

checklist.step: Screen the producer side from the state regulatory record as well
actions: For every producer onboarding read the PDB RIRS and Administrative Actions sections and obtain the underlying orders for any action citing fraud, misappropriation or a criminal matter.
Cross-check the producer's licence application disclosures against what the orders say, since an undisclosed action is itself a character issue.
Route any felony-with-dishonesty finding into the same 1033 adjudication and consent path used for employees.
Keep the appointment unfiled and portal access denied while the adjudication runs.
Record the PDB pull date and the adjudication outcome on the producer record.
checklist.done: every producer onboarding carries a dated RIRS review and any qualifying finding is routed through the 1033 path before appointment.

checklist.step: Re-attest the existing population annually and on trigger
actions: Push an annual attestation to every in-scope employee, producer and contractor asking whether they have been convicted of a qualifying felony since their last attestation.
Track completion and escalate non-responders to their manager after 10 business days and to the Head of Compliance after 20.
Route every yes answer straight into the adjudication path with the person removed from insurance duties pending classification.
Add the trigger-based re-screen rules: promotion into a fund-handling role, return from a break in service, and any regulatory action reported by the PDB alert feed.
Record the attestation cycle completion rate and the yes-answer outcomes.
checklist.done: the annual attestation is completed and tracked to a named completion rate, with every yes answer adjudicated.

checklist.step: Keep the screening data restricted and lawful to hold
actions: Store consumer reports, court documents and adjudication records in a restricted-access area with access limited to named Compliance, HR and Legal roles and every access logged.
Apply the 7-year-after-engagement retention label and configure disposal at the end of it.
Keep the regulator-facing screening register separate from the underlying reports so a data call can be answered without releasing consumer report content.
Run a quarterly access review with the Data Protection Officer and remove anyone who no longer needs the data.
checklist.done: screening data sits in a logged, restricted store with the retention label applied and a quarterly access review performed.

checklist.step: Report screening status and attest the population monthly
actions: Publish a monthly view: starters screened before start date, screens outstanding, open adjudications, consent applications pending, and consents granted with conditions.
List by name every person currently performing insurance duties with an incomplete screen and require a same-week resolution.
Sign the monthly attestation that no known prohibited person is engaged in the business of insurance without a written consent, listing any exception.
Report exceptions and any consent denial to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: a signed monthly attestation exists that no prohibited person is engaged without consent, with named exceptions listed.

testing.step: Build the population of everyone who started in the business of insurance
actions: Extract every hire and internal transfer into an insurance function with a start date in the quarter, carrying person id, role, department, start date and hiring manager.
Add producers onboarded in the quarter from the producer management system and contractors and vendor staff from the contingent-worker register.
Apply the published in-scope definition to classify each row in or out of scope and record the reason for every out-of-scope call.
Sign the extract with the query, run date and row counts by source.
testing.done: a signed, three-source population exists with every out-of-scope classification reasoned.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to payroll, access and production evidence
actions: Compare the population to the payroll register and the contingent-worker invoices for the quarter to find people paid but never in the starter extract.
Compare to the identity platform's new-account list for underwriting, claims and policy administration systems, since a system account is proof of insurance duties.
Compare to producers who wrote business in the quarter but never appeared in an onboarding record.
List every person found by these routes but missing from the population as a completeness exception.
testing.done: the population ties to payroll, system access and production records, with every omission listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of screens with a reported conviction, 100% of people engaged under a written consent, and 100% of completeness exceptions found above.
Take 25 further people at random using a seeded draw from the cleared population, minimum 40 items overall.
Weight the judgemental portion toward contractors, roles handling premium or claim funds and rehires.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and rule.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and includes every conviction case and every consent-based engagement.

testing.step: Re-perform the timing test: screen completion against engagement
actions: For each sampled person read the screening completion date and compare it to the start date, the first system-access date and, for producers, the first application date.
Any engagement date earlier than the screen completion is an exception regardless of how the screen eventually came out.
Where a fair-chance sequencing rule delayed the criminal inquiry, confirm the delay was to the stated rule and that engagement still did not precede completion.
Capture the HRIS start-date field and the screening completion field into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled person's screen completion is proven to pre-date engagement, or an exception is raised.

testing.step: Re-perform the 1033 classification independently on every conviction case
actions: Read the certified court documents for each sampled conviction before looking at the recorded classification.
Apply the two-part test yourself — felony, and dishonesty or breach of trust or a 1033 offence — and reach your own conclusion.
Compare to the recorded classification; a NOT PROHIBITED call on a felony theft, fraud, forgery or embezzlement record is a severe exception reported immediately.
Confirm the classification was supported by certified documents rather than the vendor summary line alone.
testing.done: each conviction case carries an independent classification and any misclassification is reported on discovery.

testing.step: Trace every consent-based engagement to a written regulator consent
actions: For each person engaged despite a prohibiting conviction, produce the written consent letter from the Alaska Division of Insurance or the relevant state regulator.
Confirm the consent letter names the person and pre-dates the engagement date, and that the consenting regulator is the right one for where the person works.
Read the conditions on the letter and test that each is enforced — check the system entitlements, approval limits and fund-handling restrictions actually in place.
Confirm any time-limited consent has not expired and that a renewal is diarised.
testing.done: every consent-based engagement traces to a pre-dating written consent whose conditions are demonstrably enforced in the systems.

testing.step: Test the FCRA disclosure, authorisation and adverse action sequence
actions: For each sampled screen confirm a standalone disclosure and a signed authorisation exist and pre-date the vendor order date.

For each adverse decision confirm the pre-adverse notice went with a copy of the report and the summary of rights, and recompute the gap to the adverse action notice against the 5-business-day minimum.
Confirm any dispute or context the person supplied was recorded as considered before the final notice.
Log a missing or bundled disclosure as an exception even where the hiring outcome was correct.
testing.done: disclosure, authorisation and the recomputed pre-adverse gap are verified for every sampled adverse decision.

testing.step: Test the producer-side regulatory review and the annual re-attestation
actions: For sampled producers re-pull the PDB and read the RIRS and Administrative Actions sections yourself, comparing to the onboarding review record.
Confirm any action citing fraud or misappropriation was routed into the 1033 adjudication path before the appointment was filed.
Take the annual attestation cycle and recompute the completion rate from the raw responses, listing non-responders still performing insurance duties.
Confirm every yes answer in the cycle has an adjudication record and, where prohibiting, a consent or a removal.
testing.done: producer regulatory reviews and the attestation completion rate are independently recomputed with every yes answer traced to an outcome.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and containment
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the person by employee or producer id, the role, the duties performed and the dates of unscreened or unconsented engagement.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list — entry point bypassed the screen, contractor route not covered, classification made from the vendor summary, consent not sought, condition not enforced, attestation not completed — and name an owner.
Record the containment taken: removal from insurance duties, entitlement revocation, or consent application opened, with the date it took effect.
Refer every prohibited-person engagement to the General Counsel for the notification decision and record it either way.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, a named owner, a dated containment action and a notification decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute separate rates for engagements without a completed screen, misclassified convictions, consent-condition failures and FCRA sequence defects.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the evidence behind each rate.
Have the Internal Auditor, who adjudicated no sampled screen, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Compliance Committee and, where a prohibited person was engaged, to the Audit Committee, then file the workpaper in the restricted evidence store.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with four stated rates, a conclusion and the committee reporting dates is filed in the restricted store.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly reconciliation of the internal producer roster to the Alaska and 50-state appointment records held by the regulators, and owns the break-resolution queue that comes out of it

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alaska Statutes Title 21, Chapter 27 on appointment and termination of representatives (the state's appointment record is the legal record of who is authorised to act for the insurer) checked against the current Alaska Division of Insurance appointment renewal instructions and the NIPR Alaska state page each reconciliation cycle

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly three-way reconciliation: contracted producer roster in the producer management system, appointments held on the state record via NIPR, and producers actually writing or being paid on business in the quarter, per writing company and per state

In-scope systems.value: PDB bulk appointment extract is the regulator-side source; the agency/producer management system supplies the contracted roster and the billing/commission platform and policy administration supply the production side of the match

Compliance procedure documented.value: Producer Roster Reconciliation Procedure — extract definitions, NPN key normalisation, three-way match rules, break classification into missing appointment, orphan appointment, licence-line mismatch and unlicensed production, and the resolution and clawback rules per break type

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Distribution Operations Manager; reviewed annually and whenever a writing company is added, merged or renamed, because the appointing entity changes the whole match

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly — the reconciliation is run within 15 business days of quarter end, every break is classified within 5 business days of the run, and missing appointments or overdue terminations found by it are filed inside their own statutory windows (15 days to appoint, 30 days to terminate)

Deadline reminders configured.value: The reconciliation task opens automatically at quarter end with a 15-business-day due date; each unresolved break raises an ageing alert at day 10 and escalates to the Head of Compliance at day 20

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The dated PDB bulk extract, the roster and production extracts, the matched reconciliation file with break classifications, the resolution log and the signed sign-off, retained 5 years from the reconciliation date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Each break is logged by type with the producer NPN, writing company, state, policies and premium affected, the fee exposure on orphan appointments and the commission clawed back, with the resolution date and owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the completed reconciliation, the break population and every decision to write off a commission clawback or to leave a break open into the following quarter

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full contracted producer roster at quarter end, the full state appointment extract for the same date, and every policy and commission payment in the quarter — the reconciliation itself is the population, tested at 100% rather than sampled

Pass/fail thresholds.value: The reconciliation must be complete (every roster row and every state appointment row matched or classified) and every break classified within 5 business days; any producer who wrote business with no appointment on the state record is a fail, and any orphan appointment left live for a full further quarter is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly; the verification test is performed on each quarterly run and re-performs the match independently rather than reviewing the performer's output

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Licensing Ops and must not have built or resolved any break in the reconciliation under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly roster reconciliation test workpaper (independent extracts, re-performed match, break re-classification, exposure quantification, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Producer Licensing / Reconciliation

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The reconciliation report showing roster count, state appointment count, matched count and each break class with its resolution, producible to an Alaska market conduct examiner as the producer-licensing data call response within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Producer Compliance Manager owns the Division inquiry and the appointment data call; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission that business was written by an unappointed producer before the response is sent

checklist.step: Fix the as-of date and open the reconciliation record
actions: Set the as-of date to the last calendar day of the quarter and record it — every extract in the run must be pulled as of that same date or the breaks are artefacts of timing.
Open the reconciliation record with the quarter, the as-of date, the writing companies in scope and the states in scope (all 51 jurisdictions, with Alaska reported separately).
Name the preparer and the reviewer up front so the segregation is fixed before any data is pulled.
Diarise the 15-business-day completion date and the 5-business-day break-classification target.
checklist.done: the reconciliation record names the as-of date, scope, preparer, reviewer and both due dates.

checklist.step: Extract the contracted producer roster as of the quarter end
actions: Extract every producer and agency with an active contract on the as-of date, carrying NPN, entity or individual flag, agency parent, contract execution date, termination date if any, contracted states, contracted lines and internal producer codes.
Include producers terminated during the quarter with their termination effective date, because they are the population that generates orphan appointments.
Include every internal producer code mapped to the NPN, since one producer often carries several codes across writing companies.
Save the extract with the query text, run timestamp and row count and lock it so later edits cannot change the population.
checklist.done: a locked, timestamped roster extract exists including in-quarter terminations and every producer code alias.

checklist.step: Extract the state appointment record from NIPR for the same date
actions: Run a bulk PDB appointment extract covering every writing company NAIC code in scope, across all states, as of the quarter end.
Extract per row: producer NPN, appointing company NAIC code, state, lines of authority appointed, appointment effective date and termination date if present.
Pull the licence status, class, lines and expiry date alongside, because a live appointment against an expired licence is its own break class.
Save the extract with its pull timestamp and row count and file it as the regulator-side source of truth for the run.
checklist.done: a timestamped state appointment extract covering every writing company and state exists with licence status attached.

checklist.step: Extract the production and commission side of the match
actions: Extract every policy written or renewed in the quarter with its producer code, writing company, state, line, effective date and written premium from policy administration.
Extract every commission payment in the quarter with producer code, writing company, statement period and amount.
Translate producer codes to NPN using the alias map and flag any code that does not resolve to exactly one NPN.
Total premium and commission by producer so the exposure on any break can be quantified immediately.
checklist.done: production and commission extracts exist keyed to NPN with unresolvable producer codes flagged and totals available per producer.

checklist.step: Normalise the keys before matching anything
actions: Standardise NPN to a fixed-length numeric key with leading zeros preserved, because truncated NPNs are the most common false break.
Standardise the state code to the two-letter USPS abbreviation and the company key to the NAIC company code rather than a legal name.
Map internal line names to the state line-of-authority vocabulary using a maintained crosswalk, and list any line with no mapping.
Run duplicate checks on NPN plus company plus state in each extract and resolve duplicates before matching.
Record the normalisation rules applied and the row counts before and after.
checklist.done: all three extracts share NPN, NAIC code, state and line keys, with duplicates resolved and normalisation rules recorded.

checklist.step: Run the three-way match at the producer, company and state grain
actions: Build the match key as NPN plus appointing company NAIC code plus state, and full-outer-join roster, state appointments and production.

Emit a matched set and four break sets: roster with no state appointment, state appointment with no active roster row, production with no state appointment, and appointment present but line of authority not covering the line written.
Prove the arithmetic on the face of the report: roster rows = matched + roster-only, and state rows = matched + state-only, with no residual.
Publish the counts and the reconciling arithmetic in the reconciliation report header so nothing can be quietly dropped.
Attach the break sets as separate worklists.
checklist.done: the match runs with reconciling arithmetic shown, and four named break sets are produced as worklists.

checklist.step: Classify and prioritise every break within five business days
actions: Classify each break: MISSING APPOINTMENT (contracted and producing but not appointed), ORPHAN APPOINTMENT (appointed at the state but terminated or never contracted internally), LINE MISMATCH (appointed but not for the line written), LICENCE ISSUE (appointment live against an expired or inactive licence), DATA BREAK (key or alias problem, no regulatory consequence).
Prioritise every break carrying production or commission in the quarter to the top of the queue, because those carry live regulatory exposure.
Assign each break an owner and a resolution date inside the statutory window that applies to its fix.
Record the classification reasoning per break so the same break is not re-argued next quarter.
checklist.done: every break carries a class from the fixed list, an owner, a resolution date and recorded reasoning, within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Clear missing appointments and quantify what was written without one
actions: For each MISSING APPOINTMENT break confirm the licence is active and the company is authorised, then file the appointment transaction in NIPR immediately and capture the reference.
Compute the exposure: the applications, bound policies and premium attributed to that producer and company between the contract or first-application date and the new appointment effective date.
Where production occurred in the gap, raise the exception separately from the reconciliation break so it is not closed by the mere act of appointing.
Suspend the producer's ability to write further business for that company until the state record shows the appointment active.
checklist.done: each missing appointment is filed and the production written in the gap is quantified as its own exception.

checklist.step: Terminate orphan appointments and recover the wasted renewal fees
actions: For each ORPHAN APPOINTMENT check the roster for a termination event; where one exists, establish why the NIPR termination was never filed or was rejected.
File the termination transaction with the correct effective date and reason code, and confirm whether the case is for-cause, which brings the reporting duty with it.
Compute the appointment renewal fees paid on orphan appointments since the internal termination date and report the amount to the Distribution Operations Manager.
Confirm no business was submitted under that producer code after the internal termination date, and raise an exception if it was.
Re-pull the PDB after filing to confirm the appointment actually came off the state record.
checklist.done: every orphan appointment is terminated at the state, the wasted fee is quantified and post-termination production is checked.

checklist.step: Resolve line-of-authority mismatches against what was actually sold
actions: For each LINE MISMATCH list the policies written in the unappointed or unlicensed line with premium and dates.
Establish whether the producer held the line at licence level but was not appointed for it, or did not hold the line at all — the second is the more serious.
File the appointment line addition where the licence supports it, and remove the product from the producer's portal entitlement where it does not.
Refer any policy written in a line the producer never held to Regulatory Counsel for a validity and self-report assessment.
Record the resolution and the entitlement change reference on the break.
checklist.done: each line mismatch is resolved by appointment addition or entitlement removal, with unlicensed-line policies referred to counsel.

checklist.step: Act on appointments sitting against inactive or expired licences
actions: For each LICENCE ISSUE break suspend portal access and set the commission hold on the day the break is classified.
Determine whether the licence lapsed, was cancelled or was revoked, and route lapses into the renewal or reinstatement path and revocations into the termination path.
Where the licence is revoked or suspended for cause, treat the termination as for-cause and follow the Uniform Notice of Termination route.
Quantify any production after the licence became inactive and raise it as a separate exception.
checklist.done: every appointment against an inactive licence has access stopped, a routed remedy and quantified post-lapse production.

checklist.step: Execute the commission consequences of the breaks
actions: For each break carrying commission paid to an unappointed or unlicensed producer, compute the amount by statement period.
Raise the clawback against the producer or agency account per the producer agreement and record the recovery schedule.
Where the clawback is written off, require the Head of Compliance's sign-off with the reason and the amount, since a write-off is a decision and not an outcome.
Confirm the commission-hold rule that should have prevented the payment and, where it did not fire, raise a control defect against it.
checklist.done: every improper commission is quantified and either recovered on a schedule or written off with named sign-off, with control defects raised.

checklist.step: Fix the root causes rather than only the rows
actions: Group the quarter's breaks by root cause: termination event never raised, NIPR rejection not worked, alias map wrong, new writing company not added to the extract, line crosswalk missing an entry.
For each cause with more than a handful of breaks, raise a process or system change with an owner and a delivery date rather than a manual fix.
Compare cause volumes to the previous two quarters to show whether a fix actually worked.
Report the top three causes and their fixes in the reconciliation sign-off pack.
checklist.done: breaks are grouped by cause, repeat causes carry a dated systemic fix, and the trend against prior quarters is shown.

checklist.step: Publish the reconciliation report and obtain sign-off
actions: Publish the report showing roster count, state appointment count, matched count, each break class with counts and premium exposure, and the reconciling arithmetic.
Report Alaska separately alongside the all-states totals, since the state-level position is what an Alaska examiner will ask for.
Review the open breaks with the Distribution Operations Manager and agree owners and dates for anything carried forward.
Sign the reconciliation as complete, naming the breaks left open and why, and route the pack to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation report exists with reconciling arithmetic, Alaska reported separately and every carried-forward break named.

checklist.step: Bank the reconciliation evidence and seed the next quarter
actions: File the locked extracts, the matched file, the break worklists with classifications, the resolution log and the signed report under Producer Licensing / Reconciliation with the as-of date.
Apply the 5-year retention label and confirm the record is searchable by quarter, state, writing company and NPN.
Carry every unresolved break into the next quarter's run as a mandatory opening item so it cannot be re-derived and re-aged from zero.
Update the procedure with any new break class or normalisation rule the quarter revealed.
checklist.done: the reconciliation pack is filed under retention, and unresolved breaks are seeded as opening items in the next quarter's run.

testing.step: Rebuild the three populations independently as of the same date
actions: Re-extract the contracted roster, the state appointment record and the production and commission data as of the same quarter-end date, writing your own queries rather than reusing the performer's.
Compare your row counts to the performer's locked extracts and investigate any difference before going further.
Confirm the state extract covers every writing company NAIC code that appears in the policy register, since a missing company hides an entire block of breaks.
Sign the re-extracts with queries, timestamps and row counts.
testing.done: three independently rebuilt extracts exist and their counts are reconciled to the performer's locked versions.

testing.step: Verify the state-side extract really is the regulator record
actions: Select 15 producers from the state extract and re-query each NPN individually in the PDB, reading the Alaska appointment rows on screen.
Compare appointing company, state, lines, effective date and any termination date to the bulk extract row.
Confirm the bulk extract was pulled as of the quarter end and not refreshed later, by checking the pull timestamp against the as-of date.
Log any difference as a source-integrity finding, because every downstream break depends on this extract.
testing.done: 15 individually re-queried producers agree with the bulk extract and the pull timestamp matches the as-of date.

testing.step: Re-perform the match with your own keys and prove the arithmetic
actions: Normalise NPN, NAIC code, state and line yourself and full-outer-join the three populations on NPN plus company plus state.
Recompute matched, roster-only, state-only, production-only and line-mismatch counts and compare each to the performer's report.
Prove roster rows = matched + roster-only and state rows = matched + state-only in your own file, and investigate any residual.
Test the alias map by checking that every producer code in the production extract resolves to exactly one NPN in your version too.
testing.done: the independently re-performed match reproduces every break count with the arithmetic proved in the auditor's own file.

testing.step: Re-classify a sample of breaks without reading the performer's call
actions: Take 100% of breaks carrying production or commission and 25 further breaks at random using a seeded draw, minimum 40 items.
Classify each into missing appointment, orphan appointment, line mismatch, licence issue or data break from the underlying records alone.
Compare to the performer's classification; a regulatory break classified as a data break is an exception reported immediately.
Record the seed, the population and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is independently re-classified and every downgrade to data break is challenged.

testing.step: Test that resolutions actually landed on the state record
actions: For each sampled resolved break re-pull the PDB and confirm the appointment now exists, or no longer exists, as the resolution claims.
Confirm the appointment effective date or termination date on the state record matches what the resolution log says was filed.
Treat a resolution logged as closed with no corresponding state record change as an open break, not a closed one.
Capture the PDB page for each tested resolution into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled resolution is confirmed on the state record with matching dates, or is reopened.

testing.step: Recompute the exposure attached to each production-carrying break
actions: For each break with production, recompute the policy count, written premium and commission between the start of the gap and the date the state record was corrected.
Compare to the exposure the performer recorded and investigate any understatement.
Confirm the gap start date is the earlier of contract execution and first application, not the date the break was discovered.
Trace one policy per break end to end from application to commission payment to prove the exposure is real.
testing.done: exposure is independently recomputed for every production-carrying break, with the gap start proved and one policy traced per break.

testing.step: Test the statutory windows on the fixes the reconciliation generated
actions: For appointments filed as a result of the reconciliation, recompute the original 15-day window from the contract or first-application date and record how far outside it the filing was.
For terminations filed as a result of the reconciliation, recompute the 30-day window from the termination effective date and record the days late.
Confirm every for-cause case found among the orphan appointments was filed on the Uniform Notice of Termination with the narrative, not as a plain cancellation.
Confirm the producer copy of each termination was sent within 15 days of the filing with proof of dispatch.
testing.done: each reconciliation-driven filing has a recomputed day count and every for-cause case is confirmed as properly notified.

testing.step: Test the commission clawbacks and write-offs
actions: For each break with improper commission, trace the clawback to the producer account entry and the recovery schedule.
Confirm every write-off carries the Head of Compliance's named sign-off with the amount and reason, and recompute the total written off in the quarter.
Test whether the commission-hold rule fired on a controlled unappointed test case, to prove the preventive control works and not just the detective one.
List any payment released by supervisor override during the quarter.
testing.done: clawbacks trace to account entries, write-offs carry named sign-off, and the preventive commission hold is proved to fire.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and systemic consequence
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each testing exception with the break reference, NPN, company, state, exposure and what the re-performance found.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list — extract scope missed a company, key normalisation wrong, break misclassified, resolution logged without a state change, exposure understated, window missed — and name an owner.
Where the same root cause appears for a third consecutive quarter, raise it as a control design failure rather than an operating failure.
Refer unappointed-production findings to Regulatory Counsel for an Alaska Division notification decision and record the outcome.
testing.done: every testing exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner and, where repeated, a design-failure escalation.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the completeness rate of the reconciliation, the classification accuracy rate from the re-classification sample, and the resolution-confirmed rate from the state re-pull.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the evidence behind each rate and stating the residual unappointed-production exposure.
Have the Internal Auditor, who built and resolved no break in the reconciliation under test, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper with the reconciliation pack in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with three stated rates, the residual exposure, a conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.
